_comment: SURGX media registry AND THE LICENCE GATE. Absence of a licence record is a REFUSAL, not a default-allow (assets/kardiox-learn/ holds 872 images with no manifest and no licence record; that is the failure mode this exists to prevent). An uncleared entry is a WORK ORDER: it must say what is needed and where to look, and it renders as a caption plus 'visual pending' until it is cleared. Only self-authored inline SVG is cleared today, because it is the one kind of media that needs no sourcing and whose provenance we can honestly assert.

med.surgx.appendix-anatomy.title: Finding the appendix
med.surgx.appendix-anatomy.caption: The three taeniae coli converge on the base of the appendix. Following one distally locates the base whatever the position of the tip.

med.surgx.calot-triangle.title: The hepatocystic triangle
med.surgx.calot-triangle.caption: Bounded by the cystic duct, the common hepatic duct and the inferior border of the liver. Lateral traction on the infundibulum opens it; cephalad traction closes it and aligns the cystic duct with the common bile duct.

med.surgx.cvs-diagram.title: The Critical View of Safety
med.surgx.cvs-diagram.caption: Three criteria, all required: the hepatocystic triangle cleared of fat and fibrous tissue, the lower third of the gallbladder separated from the cystic plate, and exactly two structures entering the gallbladder.

med.surgx.inguinal-canal.title: Direct, indirect and femoral
med.surgx.inguinal-canal.caption: The inferior epigastric vessels separate an indirect hernia (lateral, through the deep ring) from a direct one (medial, through Hesselbach triangle). A femoral hernia passes below the inguinal ligament, medial to the vein.

med.surgx.lap-quadrants.title: The exploration sequence
med.surgx.lap-quadrants.caption: The same order every time: supracolic, small bowel from the duodenojejunal flexure to the caecum, colon, both paracolic gutters, pelvis, retroperitoneum. The numbering is the point.

med.surgx.appendix-base.caption: Endoscopic view of the appendix base cleared circumferentially, with healthy caecal wall visible on both sides before an endoloop is applied.
med.surgx.appendix-base.note: WORK ORDER: an intra-operative still showing a properly cleared base. Source it either from an openly licensed surgical atlas (CC BY or CC0 only) or produce it in-house with documented patient consent for educational use. Do NOT take a frame from a commercial atlas or a YouTube video.

med.surgx.abscess-deloculation.caption: A multiloculated abscess cavity in cross-section, showing why a single stab incision drains only one compartment.
med.surgx.abscess-deloculation.note: WORK ORDER: authorable in-house as an inline SVG in surgx-diagrams.js, in the same style as the other five. Until it is drawn it stays refused. Estimated effort: one diagram.

med.surgx.cvs-video.caption: A narrated laparoscopic cholecystectomy demonstrating achievement of the Critical View of Safety.
med.surgx.cvs-video.note: WORK ORDER: SAGES publishes safe-cholecystectomy teaching video. Confirm the embedding terms in writing before adding videoId + embeddable:true. Do not hotlink or re-host. Note that a permitted embed also needs the /_site/yt shim on native, as CliniX documents.

med.surgx.app-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.app-step-01.caption: The site is marked by the surgeon on an awake patient, before anaesthesia.

med.surgx.app-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.app-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the knife touches skin.

med.surgx.app-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.app-step-03.caption: The antibiotic goes in before the incision, and clot prevention is in place.

med.surgx.app-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.app-step-04.caption: Head-down with left tilt: gravity clears the small bowel off the right iliac fossa.

med.surgx.app-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.app-step-05.caption: Prepare widely enough to convert or extend the incision without re-prepping.

med.surgx.app-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.app-step-06.caption: Open (Hasson) entry: the first port goes in under direct vision, clear of the bowel.

med.surgx.app-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.app-step-07.caption: Working ports on the left, aimed at the right iliac fossa, avoiding the abdominal wall vessels.

med.surgx.app-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.app-step-08.caption: Survey the terminal ileum, pelvis and ovaries before committing to the appendix.

med.surgx.app-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.app-step-09.caption: Grasp the caecum, not the appendix, and follow the taenia coli to the base.

med.surgx.app-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.app-step-10.caption: Control the mesoappendix and appendicular artery close to the appendix, before the base.

med.surgx.app-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.app-step-11.caption: Two endoloops on healthy caecal wall, then divide above them leaving a short cuff.

med.surgx.app-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.app-step-12.caption: Aspirate contamination where it pools; do not spread it.

med.surgx.app-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.app-step-13.caption: An infected appendix leaves in a retrieval bag and never touches the wound.

med.surgx.app-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.app-step-14.caption: Check the stump and the mesoappendix for bleeding before closing.

med.surgx.app-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.app-step-15.caption: The count is a two-person check, done before closing.

med.surgx.app-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.app-step-16.caption: Every appendix goes to histology, labelled at hand-off and checked aloud.

med.surgx.app-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.app-step-17.caption: Close the fascia at every port of 10 mm or more to prevent a port-site hernia.

med.surgx.app-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.app-step-18.caption: Tension-free skin closure and a dressing that stays on for 48 hours.

med.surgx.app-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.app-step-19.caption: Write the note at once and hand over the plan in person.

med.surgx.chole-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.chole-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and site with the awake patient.

med.surgx.chole-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.chole-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before incision.

med.surgx.chole-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.chole-step-03.caption: Antibiotic within the hour before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.chole-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.chole-step-05.caption: Prepare wide enough to convert to open.

med.surgx.chole-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.chole-step-06.caption: Safe entry; open entry when in doubt.

med.surgx.chole-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.chole-step-07.caption: Ports a hand's breadth apart, placed under vision.

med.surgx.chole-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.chole-step-08.caption: Look everywhere before touching the target.

med.surgx.chole-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.chole-step-10.caption: The three criteria of the Critical View.

med.surgx.chole-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.chole-step-11.caption: Clip and divide only after the Critical View.

med.surgx.chole-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.chole-step-12.caption: Stay in the plane, check the bed and clips before the last attachment.

med.surgx.chole-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.chole-step-13.caption: Bag, then extraction through the largest port.

med.surgx.chole-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.chole-step-14.caption: Inspect systematically, including after releasing retraction.

med.surgx.chole-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.chole-step-17.caption: Close fascia of every 10 mm port, desufflate fully.

med.surgx.chole-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.chole-step-19.caption: Write it now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.hern-step-01.caption: Side confirmed with the awake patient.

med.surgx.hern-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.hern-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before incision.

med.surgx.hern-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.hern-step-03.caption: Antibiotic within the hour before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.hern-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.hern-step-04.caption: Supine and flat (or slightly head down), one arm out at no more than 90 degrees, strap across the thighs.

med.surgx.hern-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.hern-step-06.caption: Open along the fibres, protect the nerve beneath.

med.surgx.hern-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.hern-step-07.caption: Sling the cord, identify and preserve all three nerves.

med.surgx.hern-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.hern-step-08.caption: High dissection of the indirect sac; invert a direct one.

med.surgx.hern-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.hern-step-12.caption: Record every specimen, including none sent.

med.surgx.hern-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.hern-step-14.caption: Write it now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.cs-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.cs-step-01.caption: Consent and identity with the awake woman.

med.surgx.cs-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.cs-step-03.caption: Antibiotic BEFORE incision, not after cord clamping.

med.surgx.cs-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.cs-step-04.caption: Left lateral tilt of about 15 degrees until delivery, to take the uterus off the vena cava; arms out on padded boards.

med.surgx.cs-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.cs-step-06.caption: Blunt layered entry, open peritoneum high.

med.surgx.cs-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.cs-step-08.caption: Hand under the head plus fundal pressure.

med.surgx.cs-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.cs-step-09.caption: Uterotonic, then complete placenta and empty cavity.

med.surgx.cs-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.cs-step-11.caption: Inspect both tubes and ovaries and record.

med.surgx.cs-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.cs-step-12.caption: Check the angles and the suture line.

med.surgx.cs-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.cs-step-13.caption: Measure, not estimate; say it aloud.

med.surgx.cs-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.cs-step-15.caption: Close the sheath; fat only if over 2 cm.

med.surgx.cs-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.cs-step-17.caption: Check rhesus status and give anti-D if needed.

med.surgx.thyr-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.thyr-step-02.caption: The operation matches the MDT decision and the diagnosis.

med.surgx.thyr-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.thyr-step-04.caption: Antibiotic within the hour before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.thyr-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.thyr-step-07.caption: Flaps above the anterior jugular veins, open the midline.

med.surgx.thyr-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.thyr-step-08.caption: Get the vagal signal before dissection.

med.surgx.thyr-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.thyr-step-09.caption: Protect the external branch, tie close to the gland.

med.surgx.thyr-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.thyr-step-10.caption: Keep each parathyroid on its blood supply.

med.surgx.thyr-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.thyr-step-11.caption: Find, confirm and trace the nerve before dividing anything.

med.surgx.thyr-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.thyr-step-12.caption: Nerve in view at the most dangerous point.

med.surgx.thyr-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.thyr-step-13.caption: Confirm the signal before starting the second side.

med.surgx.thyr-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.thyr-step-14.caption: Orient the intact specimen for the pathologist.

med.surgx.thyr-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.thyr-step-15.caption: Check after a Valsalva or pressure rise.

med.surgx.thyr-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.thyr-step-19.caption: Hand over the airway and calcium plan; haematoma kit at the bed.

med.surgx.chole-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.chole-step-04.caption: Head up about 20 degrees and left side down, so the bowel falls away from the gallbladder; arms tucked, foot board and thigh strap.

med.surgx.thyr-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.thyr-step-05.caption: Shoulder roll with the neck extended to open the neck; head up about 15 degrees to reduce venous bleeding; arms tucked.

med.surgx.hmd-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.hmd-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.hmd-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.hmd-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.hmd-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.hmd-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.hmd-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.hmd-step-04.caption: Lithotomy: hips flexed about 90 degrees and abducted, legs raised together into padded stirrups, buttocks just over the end of the table, arms out no more than 90 degrees.

med.surgx.hmd-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.hmd-step-06.caption: Calculate the safe dose, infiltrate circumferentially, wait for the adrenaline.

med.surgx.hmd-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.hmd-step-08.caption: Know the two sphincters before cutting.

med.surgx.hmd-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.hmd-step-09.caption: Stop and biopsy when the findings change the diagnosis.

med.surgx.hmd-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.hmd-step-12.caption: Transfix above the dentate line, leave a cuff.

med.surgx.hmd-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.hmd-step-14.caption: Check every wound and the calibre.

med.surgx.hmd-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.hmd-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.hmd-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.hmd-step-17.caption: Soft stools, warm soaks, warning signs.

med.surgx.hmd-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.hmd-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.tons-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.tons-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.tons-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.tons-step-02.caption: The investigation that justifies the operation is on display.

med.surgx.tons-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.tons-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.tons-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.tons-step-05.caption: Agree the airway, the throat pack is a counted item.

med.surgx.tons-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.tons-step-06.caption: Supine with a shoulder roll and the head extended on a head ring; surgeon seated at the head with a headlight; both arms tucked.

med.surgx.tons-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.tons-step-07.caption: Head drape with both eyes taped and padded; only the face and mouth exposed.

med.surgx.tons-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.tons-step-08.caption: Full view, teeth protected, ventilation unchanged.

med.surgx.tons-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.tons-step-12.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.tons-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.tons-step-14.caption: Bleeding risk and what bleeding looks like.

med.surgx.tons-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.tons-step-15.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.tkr-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.tkr-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.tkr-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.tkr-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.tkr-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.tkr-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.tkr-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.tkr-step-04.caption: Ultraclean air, low traffic, implants opened late.

med.surgx.tkr-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.tkr-step-05.caption: Supine, tourniquet high on the right thigh, a foot rest holding the knee at 90 degrees, a lateral thigh post, pressure points padded.

med.surgx.tkr-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.tkr-step-06.caption: Apply, decide aloud, record the time.

med.surgx.tkr-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.tkr-step-08.caption: Medial arthrotomy, protect the tendon insertion.

med.surgx.tkr-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.tkr-step-09.caption: Alignment guides, protect the back of the tibia.

med.surgx.tkr-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.tkr-step-10.caption: Equal, rectangular gaps in flexion and extension.

med.surgx.tkr-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.tkr-step-11.caption: Stability and range with the trials.

med.surgx.tkr-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.tkr-step-12.caption: Confirm type, size and side aloud.

med.surgx.tkr-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.tkr-step-13.caption: Cement safety pause, dry bone, hold still while it sets.

med.surgx.tkr-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.tkr-step-14.caption: Stop when the feel changes, find the extent.

med.surgx.tkr-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.tkr-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.tkr-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.tkr-step-18.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.tkr-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.tkr-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.rhc-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.rhc-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.rhc-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.rhc-step-02.caption: The operation matches the MDT decision and the staging.

med.surgx.rhc-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.rhc-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.rhc-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.rhc-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.rhc-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.rhc-step-05.caption: Supine, both arms tucked and strapped; head down about 15 degrees and rolled left side down so the small bowel falls away from the right colon.

med.surgx.rhc-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.rhc-step-06.caption: Whole abdomen prepared from the nipple line to the groins.

med.surgx.rhc-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.rhc-step-08.caption: Ports on the LEFT, a hand's breadth apart.

med.surgx.rhc-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.rhc-step-11.caption: The mesocolic plane, duodenum identified early.

med.surgx.rhc-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.rhc-step-12.caption: Central vascular ligation, careful near the SMV.

med.surgx.rhc-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.rhc-step-13.caption: Free the colon fully, avoid the duodenum.

med.surgx.rhc-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.rhc-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.rhc-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.rhc-step-21.caption: Close every 10 mm or larger fascial defect.

med.surgx.rhc-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.rhc-step-22.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.rhc-step-23.title: Step 23
med.surgx.rhc-step-23.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.turp-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.turp-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.turp-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.turp-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.turp-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.turp-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.turp-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.turp-step-04.caption: Lithotomy under spinal anaesthesia: the patient awake, the anaesthetist at the head, irrigation bags hung low (about 60 cm).

med.surgx.turp-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.turp-step-06.caption: Inspect the whole bladder before resecting.

med.surgx.turp-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.turp-step-07.caption: Right fluid for the energy, lowest pressure, never force the sheath.

med.surgx.turp-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.turp-step-08.caption: Identify the orifices first, channel at 6 o'clock to the circular fibres.

med.surgx.turp-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.turp-step-10.caption: Never cut distal to the verumontanum.

med.surgx.turp-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.turp-step-11.caption: Watch for TUR syndrome, keep the pressure low.

med.surgx.turp-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.turp-step-12.caption: Evacuate all chips, re-inspect the bladder.

med.surgx.turp-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.turp-step-15.caption: Free drainage before inflating the balloon, light pink return.

med.surgx.turp-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.turp-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.turp-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.turp-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lapa-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lapa-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lapa-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lapa-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lapa-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.lapa-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.lapa-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lapa-step-04.caption: Supine and flat, arms at the sides, a safety strap across the thighs, heels padded, the catheter draining below the table.

med.surgx.lapa-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lapa-step-05.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.lapa-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lapa-step-06.caption: Stay in the midline, open the peritoneum under direct vision.

med.surgx.lapa-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lapa-step-08.caption: Handle with the whole hand, assess colour, peristalsis and pulsation.

med.surgx.lapa-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lapa-step-10.caption: Decide on physiology, control bleeding and contamination, close temporarily.

med.surgx.lapa-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lapa-step-11.caption: Wash out all four quadrants and the pelvis, aspirate completely.

med.surgx.lapa-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lapa-step-12.caption: Site it where the patient can see and care for it, tension-free and perfused.

med.surgx.lapa-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lapa-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lapa-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lapa-step-17.caption: Small bites, at least 4 to 1 suture to wound length.

med.surgx.lapa-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lapa-step-18.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lapa-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lapa-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.mrm-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.mrm-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.mrm-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.mrm-step-02.caption: The operation matches the MDT decision, side and extent.

med.surgx.mrm-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.mrm-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.mrm-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.mrm-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.mrm-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.mrm-step-06.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.mrm-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.mrm-step-07.caption: Raise even flaps in the mastectomy plane.

med.surgx.mrm-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.mrm-step-08.caption: Take the fascia, control the perforators.

med.surgx.mrm-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.mrm-step-10.caption: Enter the axilla through the clavipectoral fascia.

med.surgx.mrm-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.mrm-step-11.caption: Clear levels I and II, preserve both nerves, keep below the vein.

med.surgx.mrm-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.mrm-step-12.caption: Orient with the agreed convention before it leaves the field.

med.surgx.mrm-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.mrm-step-14.caption: Drain the dead space through separate stabs.

med.surgx.mrm-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.mrm-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.mrm-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.mrm-step-17.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.mrm-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.mrm-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.thr-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.thr-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.thr-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.thr-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.thr-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.thr-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.thr-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.thr-step-04.caption: Ultraclean air, low traffic, implants opened late.

med.surgx.thr-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.thr-step-05.caption: Left lateral decubitus with the pelvis held vertical by front and back supports, an axillary roll and a pillow between the legs.

med.surgx.thr-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.thr-step-06.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.thr-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.thr-step-07.caption: Reflect the rotators back to protect the sciatic nerve.

med.surgx.thr-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.thr-step-08.caption: Dislocate gently, cut at the planned level.

med.surgx.thr-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.thr-step-10.caption: Aim for the planned inclination and anteversion.

med.surgx.thr-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.thr-step-11.caption: Tibia vertical shows femoral version; increase broach size stepwise.

med.surgx.thr-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.thr-step-13.caption: Confirm type, size and side aloud.

med.surgx.thr-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.thr-step-15.caption: Clean the taper, reduce, re-check stability.

med.surgx.thr-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.thr-step-17.caption: Repair the posterior capsule and rotators to cut dislocation risk.

med.surgx.thr-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.thr-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.thr-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.thr-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.thr-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.thr-step-21.caption: Check the sciatic and common peroneal nerves and pulses before leaving theatre.

med.surgx.thr-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.thr-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.tah-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.tah-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.tah-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.tah-step-03.caption: Confirm pregnancy status and the work-up on the day.

med.surgx.tah-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.tah-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.tah-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.tah-step-06.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.tah-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.tah-step-07.caption: Open high, away from the bladder.

med.surgx.tah-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.tah-step-09.caption: Traction, divide the round ligament, open the broad ligament.

med.surgx.tah-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.tah-step-10.caption: See the ureter before taking pelvic pedicles.

med.surgx.tah-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.tah-step-11.caption: Decide conserve or remove; clamp close to the uterus when conserving.

med.surgx.tah-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.tah-step-12.caption: Push the bladder down before the lower pedicles.

med.surgx.tah-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.tah-step-13.caption: Clamp close to the uterus, the ureter is just lateral and below.

med.surgx.tah-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.tah-step-14.caption: Small bites medial to the last, secure the angles, close the vault.

med.surgx.tah-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.tah-step-15.caption: When the plane is lost, stop, call for help, consider subtotal.

med.surgx.tah-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.tah-step-17.caption: Measure, say it aloud, agree the next step.

med.surgx.tah-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.tah-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.tah-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.tah-step-20.caption: Include the angles, continuous delayed-absorbable suture.

med.surgx.tah-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.tah-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.tah-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.tah-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.cd-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.cd-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.cd-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.cd-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.cd-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.cd-step-03.caption: Sitting up at about 45 degrees with the right arm behind the head, awake and comfortable.

med.surgx.cd-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.cd-step-04.caption: Use the safe triangle, confirm with ultrasound.

med.surgx.cd-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.cd-step-05.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.cd-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.cd-step-06.caption: Go over the top of the rib, aspirate to confirm.

med.surgx.cd-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.cd-step-07.caption: Never let go of the wire.

med.surgx.cd-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.cd-step-08.caption: Blunt dissection and a finger sweep, never a trocar.

med.surgx.cd-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.cd-step-10.caption: Account for every sharp and the guidewire.

med.surgx.cd-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.cd-step-11.caption: Swinging, bubbling or draining, then an X-ray.

med.surgx.cd-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.cd-step-12.caption: Hand over what to watch and when to call.

med.surgx.mrm-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.mrm-step-05.caption: Supine with the right arm out on a padded board at 90 degrees and no more, a folded sheet under the right shoulder blade.

med.surgx.thr-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.thr-step-16.caption: Stop when the feel changes, find the extent.

med.surgx.cd-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.cd-step-09.caption: Secure it, bottle below the chest, tube under water.

med.surgx.csdh-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.csdh-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.csdh-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.csdh-step-02.caption: A fresh GCS and pupil check, the side read aloud from the scan and matched to the mark.

med.surgx.csdh-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.csdh-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.csdh-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.csdh-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.csdh-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.csdh-step-06.caption: Plan the burr holes over the thickest part of the collection, away from the midline.

med.surgx.csdh-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.csdh-step-07.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.csdh-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.csdh-step-08.caption: Perpendicular, steady pressure, let the clutch stop at the inner table.

med.surgx.csdh-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.csdh-step-09.caption: Dark fluid under pressure confirms the diagnosis; open the dura away from the brain.

med.surgx.csdh-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.csdh-step-10.caption: Irrigate gently along the dura until the return is clear.

med.surgx.csdh-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.csdh-step-11.caption: Separate stab, secure, keep the bag below the head.

med.surgx.csdh-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.csdh-step-13.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.csdh-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.csdh-step-14.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.csdh-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.csdh-step-15.caption: Write a baseline GCS and pupils and a trigger for urgent CT.

med.surgx.csdh-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.csdh-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.edh-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.edh-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.edh-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.edh-step-02.caption: Pupils and motor score immediately before induction, the side read aloud.

med.surgx.edh-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.edh-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.edh-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.edh-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.edh-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.edh-step-06.caption: A trauma flap that can be extended to a full decompression.

med.surgx.edh-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.edh-step-07.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.edh-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.edh-step-08.caption: Control the scalp edges as you go; blood loss starts here.

med.surgx.edh-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.edh-step-10.caption: Free the dura first, and make the flap big enough to expose the whole clot.

med.surgx.edh-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.edh-step-11.caption: Remove the clot AND control the source, then hitch the dura.

med.surgx.edh-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.edh-step-12.caption: Open the dura only if it is blue or tense, or the scan shows subdural blood.

med.surgx.edh-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.edh-step-13.caption: If the brain swells above the inner table, leave the bone out, and make the opening large.

med.surgx.edh-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.edh-step-14.caption: A loose duraplasty gives the swollen brain room.

med.surgx.edh-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.edh-step-15.caption: Replace the bone only if the brain is slack; hitch the dura centrally.

med.surgx.edh-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.edh-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.edh-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.edh-step-18.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.edh-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.edh-step-19.caption: A written baseline and a trigger for urgent CT.

med.surgx.edh-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.edh-step-20.caption: Record whether the flap is replaced or stored, and where.

med.surgx.evd-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.evd-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.evd-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.evd-step-02.caption: Read the ventricles and any shift before choosing the side.

med.surgx.evd-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.evd-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.evd-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.evd-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.evd-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.evd-step-05.caption: Supine with the head straight, nose to the ceiling, and the head of the table raised about 30 degrees.

med.surgx.evd-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.evd-step-06.caption: Kocher point, mid-pupillary line, just in front of the coronal suture.

med.surgx.evd-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.evd-step-07.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.evd-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.evd-step-08.caption: Keep the drill perpendicular to the skull.

med.surgx.evd-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.evd-step-09.caption: Open the dura only as much as the catheter needs.

med.surgx.evd-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.evd-step-11.caption: Zero at the tragus, measure the opening pressure, keep the system closed.

med.surgx.evd-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.evd-step-12.caption: A long tunnel and firm fixation reduce infection and pull-out.

med.surgx.evd-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.evd-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.evd-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.evd-step-15.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.evd-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.evd-step-16.caption: Re-level the drain whenever the head moves; a written trigger for calling.

med.surgx.evd-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.evd-step-17.caption: Write the opening pressure, the reference level and the drain height.

med.surgx.vps-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.vps-step-01.caption: Consent covers lifelong shunt dependence and likely revisions.

med.surgx.vps-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.vps-step-02.caption: Confirm the ventricle size, the side, the entry point and the valve chosen.

med.surgx.vps-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.vps-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.vps-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.vps-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.vps-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.vps-step-06.caption: Mark the cranial entry, the scalp incision and the abdominal incision before draping.

med.surgx.vps-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.vps-step-07.caption: Check accuracy on three bony landmarks before trusting navigation.

med.surgx.vps-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.vps-step-08.caption: One continuous field, no exposed skin along the tunnel.

med.surgx.vps-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.vps-step-09.caption: Open the implant only when needed, fresh gloves, it never touches skin.

med.surgx.vps-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.vps-step-10.caption: Curve the incision so no implant lies under the scar.

med.surgx.vps-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.vps-step-11.caption: Perpendicular, let the clutch stop at the inner table.

med.surgx.vps-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.vps-step-12.caption: Enter under vision and see omentum or bowel, not preperitoneal fat.

med.surgx.vps-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.vps-step-14.caption: A small opening so CSF does not leak around the catheter.

med.surgx.vps-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.vps-step-15.caption: One clean pass to the planned depth; if no CSF, withdraw fully, never redirect inside the brain.

med.surgx.vps-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.vps-step-16.caption: Secure every joint, valve the right way round, see spontaneous distal flow.

med.surgx.vps-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.vps-step-17.caption: Free intraperitoneal placement with enough length.

med.surgx.vps-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.vps-step-18.caption: Cloudy CSF means no implant: send CSF and place an external drain.

med.surgx.vps-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.vps-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.vps-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.vps-step-20.caption: Close the galea, and never leave an implant under the suture line.

med.surgx.vps-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.vps-step-21.caption: Headache, vomiting and drowsiness are shunt-failure triggers.

med.surgx.vps-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.vps-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ces-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.ces-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.ces-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ces-step-02.caption: Read the level from the MRI aloud and match it to the mark; record leg, saddle and bladder function.

med.surgx.ces-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.ces-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ces-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.ces-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.ces-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ces-step-05.caption: Prone on bolsters under the chest and pelvis so the abdomen hangs free, face in a padded headrest, knees padded.

med.surgx.ces-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ces-step-06.caption: Prepare widely from the incision outwards and let it dry before drapes and diathermy.

med.surgx.ces-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ces-step-07.caption: Count up from the sacrum on a lateral image before the incision.

med.surgx.ces-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ces-step-08.caption: Remove enough bone and ligament to reach the disc without pulling on a compressed sac; keep the facets.

med.surgx.ces-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ces-step-09.caption: Retract gently only once there is room; keep the rongeur at a controlled depth.

med.surgx.ces-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ces-step-10.caption: Probe under the sac, into the foramen and up and down the canal.

med.surgx.ces-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ces-step-11.caption: Repair, reinforce, test with Valsalva, tell the ward.

med.surgx.ces-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ces-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ces-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ces-step-15.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.ces-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.ces-step-16.caption: Include saddle sensation and bladder function in the baseline and the trigger for an urgent MRI.

med.surgx.ces-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.ces-step-17.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.thr-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.thr-step-12.caption: Trial head reduced into the cup: test stability and leg length with the trials before choosing implants.

med.surgx.tah-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.tah-step-05.caption: Supine with the whole table tilted head down, legs flat on the table and heels on a gel pad.

med.surgx.csdh-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.csdh-step-05.caption: Head turned to the left on a horseshoe, a roll under the right shoulder and the head raised, neck not kinked.

med.surgx.edh-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.edh-step-05.caption: Head turned to the left on a horseshoe, a roll under the right shoulder, head end raised and the jugular veins free.

med.surgx.edh-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.edh-step-09.caption: The first burr hole over the thickest clot relieves pressure.

med.surgx.evd-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.evd-step-10.caption: Aim at the medial canthus and the ear; stop after three passes.

med.surgx.vps-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.vps-step-05.caption: Head turned to the left with a roll under the right shoulder, so the tunnel runs straight from behind the ear to the abdomen.

med.surgx.vps-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.vps-step-13.caption: Stay subcutaneous and cross over the clavicle superficially.

med.surgx.phaco-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.phaco-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.phaco-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.phaco-step-02.caption: A wrong lens implant gives a large refractive surprise that needs another operation.

med.surgx.phaco-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.phaco-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.phaco-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.phaco-step-04.caption: The anaesthetic decides how still the eye is, how much the patient feels and which complications are possible.

med.surgx.phaco-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.phaco-step-05.caption: Supine with the head flat and level on a gel ring; the surgeon seated at the head with the microscope over the right eye.

med.surgx.phaco-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.phaco-step-06.caption: Endophthalmitis is the infection that loses an eye after intraocular surgery, and the bacteria come from the patient's own lids and conjunctiva.

med.surgx.phaco-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.phaco-step-07.caption: Clean the lids and skin, then an adhesive drape that tucks the lashes away.

med.surgx.phaco-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.phaco-step-08.caption: The lashes and lid margins carry the bacteria that cause endophthalmitis, and a poorly set microscope makes every later step harder.

med.surgx.phaco-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.phaco-step-09.caption: A well-built tunnel incision self-seals at the end and keeps the chamber stable.

med.surgx.phaco-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.phaco-step-10.caption: A round, central, continuous tear of the anterior capsule about 5 to 5.5 mm wide resists tearing out during phaco and holds the implant centred.

med.surgx.phaco-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.phaco-step-11.caption: Freeing the lens from its capsule lets the nucleus rotate, so it can be removed with less stress on the zonules and the posterior capsule.

med.surgx.phaco-step-12.title: Step 12

med.surgx.evis-step-18.caption: The conformer holds the fornices open so a prosthesis can be fitted later; the pressure dressing limits swelling and bleeding.

med.surgx.evis-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.evis-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.strab-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.strab-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.strab-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.strab-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.strab-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.strab-step-03.caption: The anaesthetic decides how still the eye is, how much the patient feels and which complications are possible.

med.surgx.strab-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.strab-step-04.caption: Supine with the head flat and level on a gel ring; the surgeon seated at the head with the microscope over the right eye.

med.surgx.strab-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.strab-step-05.caption: Endophthalmitis is the infection that loses an eye after intraocular surgery, and the bacteria come from the patient's own lids and conjunctiva.

med.surgx.strab-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.strab-step-06.caption: Clean the lids and skin, then an adhesive drape that tucks the lashes away.

med.surgx.strab-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.strab-step-07.caption: The lashes and lid margins carry the bacteria that cause endophthalmitis, and a poorly set microscope makes every later step harder.

med.surgx.strab-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.strab-step-08.caption: A restricted eye (thyroid, scarring, fracture) behaves differently from a weak muscle; the plan changes if passive movement is limited.

med.surgx.strab-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.strab-step-09.caption: Conjunctiva is the covering that protects a bleb, a muscle repair or an implant.

med.surgx.strab-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.strab-step-10.caption: The whole muscle must be on the hook: a split muscle is undercorrected and may slip.

med.surgx.strab-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.strab-step-11.caption: A secure locking suture through the muscle before it is cut is what stops the muscle being lost into the orbit.

med.surgx.strab-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.strab-step-12.caption: Moving the insertion back weakens the muscle by a measured amount.

med.surgx.strab-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.strab-step-13.caption: Removing a measured length and reattaching at the original insertion strengthens the muscle.

med.surgx.strab-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.strab-step-14.caption: Traction on an extraocular muscle can slow the heart abruptly, especially in children.

med.surgx.strab-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.strab-step-15.caption: A muscle that retracts into the orbit becomes hard to find quickly; a calm, structured search through Tenon's usually recovers it.

med.surgx.strab-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.strab-step-16.caption: A conjunctival closure has to cover what lies under it: a leak over a bleb drains the eye flat, and an exposed suture or implant becomes infected.

med.surgx.strab-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.strab-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.strab-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.strab-step-18.caption: Most sight-threatening problems after eye surgery declare themselves at home: increasing pain, redness and falling vision mean endophthalmitis or raised pressure until proven otherwise.

med.surgx.strab-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.strab-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ppv-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.ppv-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.ppv-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ppv-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ppv-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.ppv-step-03.caption: The anaesthetic decides how still the eye is, how much the patient feels and which complications are possible.

med.surgx.ppv-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.ppv-step-04.caption: Supine with the head flat and level on a gel ring; the surgeon seated at the head with the microscope over the right eye.

med.surgx.ppv-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ppv-step-05.caption: Endophthalmitis is the infection that loses an eye after intraocular surgery, and the bacteria come from the patient's own lids and conjunctiva.

med.surgx.ppv-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ppv-step-06.caption: Clean the lids and skin, then an adhesive drape that tucks the lashes away.

med.surgx.ppv-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ppv-step-07.caption: The lashes and lid margins carry the bacteria that cause endophthalmitis, and a poorly set microscope makes every later step harder.

med.surgx.ppv-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ppv-step-08.caption: The infusion maintains the eye's pressure throughout.

med.surgx.ppv-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ppv-step-09.caption: Removing the vitreous relieves traction on the retina.

med.surgx.ppv-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ppv-step-10.caption: The retina must be flat and every break sealed with laser or cryotherapy, or it will detach again.

med.surgx.ppv-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ppv-step-11.caption: The gas or oil holds the retina against the wall while the laser scars mature.

med.surgx.ppv-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ppv-step-12.caption: Bleeding into the suprachoroidal space can push the eye contents out of an open wound within minutes.

med.surgx.ppv-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ppv-step-13.caption: A leaking wound lets bacteria in and lets the eye go soft; a pressure that is too high hurts and can close the retinal circulation.

med.surgx.ppv-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ppv-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ppv-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ppv-step-15.caption: Most sight-threatening problems after eye surgery declare themselves at home: increasing pain, redness and falling vision mean endophthalmitis or raised pressure until proven otherwise.

med.surgx.ppv-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.ppv-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.evis-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.evis-step-16.caption: A dry scleral shell before the implant goes in.

med.surgx.sics-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.sics-step-10.caption: The nucleus has to come out of the bag, so the opening must be large enough to let it prolapse without tearing round to the posterior capsule.

med.surgx.sics-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.sics-step-14.caption: A tear in the posterior capsule is the commonest serious complication of cataract surgery.

med.surgx.sics-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.sics-step-15.caption: Bleeding into the suprachoroidal space can push the eye contents out of an open wound within minutes.

med.surgx.lasik-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lasik-step-09.caption: A flap cut through after suction loss can be irregular, thin or incomplete.

med.surgx.lasik-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lasik-step-12.caption: A treatment that has gone off centre or stopped half way cannot simply be repeated from the start.

med.surgx.ptg-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ptg-step-12.caption: Unexpected findings change the operation: thin sclera may need a patch, a damaged muscle needs repair, and a lesion that looks like neoplasia needs a different, no-touch excision with margins.

med.surgx.tx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.tx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.tx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.tx-step-02.caption: Transplanting into the wrong recipient, or across an incompatible blood group, can cause hyperacute rejection.

med.surgx.tx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.tx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.tx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.tx-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.tx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.tx-step-05.caption: Supine, arms out, a catheter ready to fill the bladder, the right iliac fossa incision marked.

med.surgx.tx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.tx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.tx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.tx-step-07.caption: Preparing the kidney on ice prevents warm injury and shows the vessels and ureter so the anastomoses are planned before the clamps go on.

med.surgx.tx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.tx-step-08.caption: The iliac fossa gives a retroperitoneal bed close to the bladder.

med.surgx.tx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.tx-step-09.caption: An artery opened without control bleeds at arterial pressure into a field you can no longer see.

med.surgx.tx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.tx-step-10.caption: The venous anastomosis is usually done first.

med.surgx.tx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.tx-step-11.caption: Most early graft and fistula failures are technical and sit at an anastomosis: a narrowed heel or toe, a lifted intimal flap, a purse-stringed suture line or a twisted conduit.

med.surgx.tx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.tx-step-12.caption: Declamping releases cold, acidic, potassium-rich blood into the circulation and drops the pressure suddenly.

med.surgx.tx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.tx-step-13.caption: A technically perfect anastomosis with a thrombosed or embolised distal bed is a failed operation.

med.surgx.tx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.tx-step-14.caption: Patchy, soft or dusky perfusion after reperfusion means a technical problem until proven otherwise, and it is reversible only while the patient is still on the table.

med.surgx.tx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.tx-step-15.caption: A short, well- vascularised ureter joined to the bladder with an anti-reflux tunnel (Lich-Gregoir) gives the fewest leaks and stenoses.

med.surgx.tx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.tx-step-18.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.tx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.tx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.tx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.tx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.tx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.tx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ldn-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.ldn-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.ldn-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ldn-step-02.caption: The donor gains nothing medically, so every safeguard is checked again on the day: identity, legal authorisation, free consent and the anatomy that was planned.

med.surgx.ldn-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.ldn-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ldn-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.ldn-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.ldn-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ldn-step-05.caption: Right side down in the flank position, table flexed, axillary roll, padded and strapped.

med.surgx.ldn-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ldn-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.ldn-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ldn-step-07.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.ldn-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ldn-step-08.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.ldn-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ldn-step-09.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.ldn-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ldn-step-10.caption: A colorectal anastomosis must lie in the pelvis without tension.

med.surgx.ldn-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ldn-step-11.caption: The ureter's blood supply runs in the tissue around it.

med.surgx.ldn-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ldn-step-14.caption: Warm ischaemia starts when the artery is stapled.

med.surgx.ldn-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.ldn-step-16.caption: In upper abdominal surgery the large veins (portal, superior mesenteric, splenic, hepatic and the cava) tear rather than cut, and clamping blindly makes a small hole large.

med.surgx.ldn-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.ldn-step-18.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.ldn-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.ldn-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ldn-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.ldn-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.avr-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.avr-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.avr-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.avr-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.avr-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.avr-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.avr-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.avr-step-04.caption: Supine, arms by the sides, chest exposed from neck to umbilicus, lines in.

med.surgx.avr-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.avr-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.avr-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.avr-step-07.caption: Gradual retraction avoids rib fractures and brachial plexus stretch, and a controlled pericardiotomy exposes the heart without injuring the innominate vein, the phrenic nerves or the heart itself.

med.surgx.avr-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.avr-step-08.caption: Bypass lets the heart be stopped and opened.

med.surgx.avr-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.avr-step-09.caption: Cardioplegia arrests and protects the heart.

med.surgx.avr-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.avr-step-10.caption: Calcium must be removed to seat the prosthesis, but fragments that fall into the ventricle or coronaries cause stroke or infarction.

med.surgx.avr-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.avr-step-11.caption: Correct sizing avoids patient-prosthesis mismatch; suture depth near the conduction tissue decides whether the patient needs a pacemaker.

med.surgx.avr-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.avr-step-12.caption: A properly seated valve does not leak around its edge or block a coronary ostium; mechanical leaflets must move freely.

med.surgx.avr-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.avr-step-13.caption: Air left in the left heart embolises to the brain or the right coronary artery when the heart starts to eject.

med.surgx.avr-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.avr-step-14.caption: Transoesophageal echo confirms the valve works before decannulation, when it can still be fixed.

med.surgx.avr-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.avr-step-15.caption: Protamine reduces wound and mediastinal bleeding, but it can cause severe hypotension, pulmonary hypertension or anaphylaxis, and given at the wrong moment it clots the repair or the bypass circuit.

med.surgx.avr-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.avr-step-16.caption: Conduction and rhythm disturbances are common after cardiac surgery, and a wire placed now is far safer than an emergency transvenous wire later.

med.surgx.avr-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.avr-step-17.caption: A drain that is kinked, blocked or wrongly placed gives false reassurance while blood or air collects, and retained blood after cardiac or thoracic surgery causes tamponade, a trapped lung and empyema.

med.surgx.avr-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.avr-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.avr-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.avr-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pw-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.pw-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.pw-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.pw-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.pw-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.pw-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.pw-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.pw-step-04.caption: Supine with the head of the table raised about 30 degrees.

med.surgx.pw-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.pw-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pw-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.pw-step-06.caption: General anaesthesia and positive pressure ventilation reduce venous return; in tamponade this can stop the circulation.

med.surgx.pw-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.pw-step-12.caption: A tear in the right ventricle or a coronary vessel bleeds massively; the window does not give enough access to repair it.

med.surgx.pw-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.pw-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.pw-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.pw-step-15.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.pw-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.pw-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.esc-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.esc-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.esc-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.esc-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.esc-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.esc-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.esc-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.esc-step-04.caption: Supine on a warmed table, the burnt left arm out on a board, the chest bare.

med.surgx.esc-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.esc-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.esc-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.esc-step-06.caption: Escharotomy is for constriction by full-thickness burn; doing it on partial-thickness burns adds wounds without benefit, and missing it costs limbs or ventilation.

med.surgx.esc-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.esc-step-08.caption: The hand is the most common place for an escharotomy to be needed and also the easiest place to injure nerves and tendons.

med.surgx.esc-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.esc-step-09.caption: A stiff burned chest wall cannot expand; releasing it as a mobile shield restores ventilation within minutes.

med.surgx.esc-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.esc-step-13.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.esc-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.esc-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.esc-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.esc-step-15.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.rhomb-step-06.caption: A rhomboid flap works only if it borrows skin from where it is lax.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.rhomb-step-07.caption: Infiltration with adrenaline gives anaesthesia and a drier field; waiting for the vasoconstriction makes the dissection easier.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.rhomb-step-08.caption: The excision follows the marked rhombus and the oncological margin; it is checked before any flap is raised.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.rhomb-step-09.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.rhomb-step-10.caption: A random-pattern flap lives on the subdermal plexus at its base; raising it in the right plane keeps that intact.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.rhomb-step-11.caption: The key stitch closes the donor site first; once that is closed, the flap should fall into the defect with little tension.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.rhomb-step-13.caption: Deep dermal sutures take the tension so the skin sutures only align the edges; this gives the best scar and protects the flap tip.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.rhomb-step-14.caption: A flap that is white or blue at the end of surgery is under tension or kinked.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.rhomb-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.rhomb-step-16.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.cleft-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.cleft-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the parents.

med.surgx.cleft-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.cleft-step-02.caption: Infants decompensate quickly and tolerate an uncorrected metabolic, glucose or temperature problem badly.

med.surgx.cleft-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.cleft-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.cleft-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.cleft-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.cleft-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.cleft-step-05.caption: Infants have a large surface area for their mass and little subcutaneous fat.

med.surgx.cleft-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.cleft-step-06.caption: A baby supine on a warming mattress, shoulder roll, head on a ring, tube taped in the midline.

med.surgx.cleft-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.cleft-step-07.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.cleft-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.cleft-step-08.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.cleft-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.cleft-step-09.caption: The repair is only as good as its marks.

med.surgx.cleft-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.cleft-step-10.caption: Wound infiltration or a regional block reduces opioid need, and opioids increase the risk of post-operative apnoea in infants.

med.surgx.cleft-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.cleft-step-11.caption: The incisions create the flaps that lengthen the medial side and bring the lateral side across; the lateral lip must be released enough to close without tension.

med.surgx.cleft-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.cleft-step-12.caption: The cleft-side alar cartilage is displaced; repositioning it at the first operation improves nasal symmetry as the child grows.

med.surgx.cleft-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.cleft-step-13.caption: The muscle is the functional core of the lip.

med.surgx.cleft-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.cleft-step-14.caption: Exact alignment of the white roll and the vermilion-mucosa junction is what people see; a small step is visible for life.

med.surgx.cleft-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.cleft-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.cleft-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.cleft-step-17.caption: A retained throat pack or a clot in the nasopharynx sitting above the larynx can obstruct the airway completely after extubation.

med.surgx.tx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.tx-step-16.caption: A stent drains an obstructed or injured ureter, but a stent in the wrong place either drains nothing or causes pain, haematuria and migration.

med.surgx.ldn-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ldn-step-13.caption: Length on the artery helps the recipient anastomosis.

med.surgx.ldn-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ldn-step-15.caption: The vascular division is the most dangerous moment for the donor: the arterial stump must be secure, and the kidney must come out quickly.

med.surgx.ldn-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.ldn-step-17.caption: The kidney is cooled and flushed at once; meanwhile the donor's vascular stumps and the field are checked under lower pneumoperitoneum.

med.surgx.avr-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.avr-step-06.caption: A sternotomy that wanders off the midline produces a weak, asymmetric closure and is the commonest technical root of sternal dehiscence.

med.surgx.pw-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.pw-step-07.caption: The subxiphoid route reaches the inferior pericardium without opening the sternum or the pleura.

med.surgx.pw-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.pw-step-08.caption: The pericardium is opened under direct vision so the fluid escapes and the heart falls away from the knife.

med.surgx.pw-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.pw-step-09.caption: Excising a piece of pericardium both prevents early closure and provides tissue for diagnosis.

med.surgx.pw-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.pw-step-11.caption: A drain that is kinked, blocked or wrongly placed gives false reassurance while blood or air collects, and retained blood after cardiac or thoracic surgery causes tamponade, a trapped lung and empyema.

med.surgx.esc-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.esc-step-12.caption: An abscess cavity closed primarily becomes an abscess again.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.rhomb-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.rhomb-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.rhomb-step-03.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.rhomb-step-04.caption: Supine, head turned to the left on a head ring so the right cheek faces up.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.rhomb-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.rhomb-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.rhomb-step-17.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.cleft-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.cleft-step-18.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.cleft-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.cleft-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.pyelo-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.pyelo-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.pyelo-step-03.caption: Instrumenting infected urine can cause urosepsis within hours.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.pyelo-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.pyelo-step-05.caption: Flank position, left side up at 45 to 60 degrees, padded, strapped, table flexed.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.pyelo-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.pyelo-step-07.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.pyelo-step-08.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.pyelo-step-09.caption: The patient cannot be moved once the robot is docked, and steep positions load the face, shoulders and legs.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.pyelo-step-10.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.pyelo-step-11.caption: Seeing the whole junction and its relation to a lower pole vessel decides the repair.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.pyelo-step-13.caption: A stent drains an obstructed or injured ureter, but a stent in the wrong place either drains nothing or causes pain, haematuria and migration.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.pyelo-step-14.caption: A watertight, tension-free and dependent anastomosis drains well and does not leak.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.pyelo-step-16.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.pyelo-step-17.caption: A forgotten stent encrusts, obstructs and can cost the kidney.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.pyelo-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.pyelo-step-19.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.pyelo-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.pn-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.pn-step-10.caption: The artery must be controlled before the tumour is cut.

med.surgx.pn-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.pn-step-14.caption: The inner layer closes opened vessels and the collecting system; the outer layer brings the kidney edges together and stops bleeding.

med.surgx.pn-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.pn-step-16.caption: In upper abdominal surgery the large veins (portal, superior mesenteric, splenic, hepatic and the cava) tear rather than cut, and clamping blindly makes a small hole large.

med.surgx.pn-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.pn-step-18.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.pn-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.pn-step-20.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.rp-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.rp-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.rp-step-05.caption: Lithotomy in steep head-down tilt, arms tucked and padded, secured against sliding, eyes protected.

med.surgx.rp-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.rp-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.rp-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.rp-step-07.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.rp-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.rp-step-08.caption: The patient cannot be moved once the robot is docked, and steep positions load the face, shoulders and legs.

med.surgx.rp-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.rp-step-09.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.rp-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.rp-step-10.caption: Opening the space in front of the bladder exposes the front of the prostate and the endopelvic fascia.

med.surgx.rp-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.rp-step-11.caption: Finding the junction of bladder and prostate right preserves the bladder neck and keeps away from the ureteric orifices.

med.surgx.rp-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.rp-step-12.caption: The vasa and seminal vesicles lead to the plane behind the prostate, in front of the rectum.

med.surgx.rp-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.rp-step-13.caption: The neurovascular bundles run beside the prostate.

med.surgx.rp-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.rp-step-14.caption: The apex is where positive margins and incontinence are decided.

med.surgx.rp-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.rp-step-15.caption: A rectal injury recognised now and repaired heals; one missed becomes a rectourethral fistula.

med.surgx.rp-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.rp-step-16.caption: A lymphadenectomy stages the cancer and, in several cancers, controls regional disease.

med.surgx.rp-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.rp-step-17.caption: A watertight, tension-free join of the bladder neck to the urethra lets the catheter come out on time and lowers stricture risk.

med.surgx.rp-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.rp-step-20.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.rp-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.rp-step-21.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.rp-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.rp-step-22.caption: After urethral or bladder surgery the catheter splints the repair.

med.surgx.rp-step-23.title: Step 23
med.surgx.rp-step-23.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.rc-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.rc-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.rc-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.rc-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.rc-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.rc-step-03.caption: Most stoma leaks, skin problems and appliance failures trace back to where the stoma was put.

med.surgx.rc-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.rc-step-04.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.rc-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.rc-step-05.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.rc-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.rc-step-06.caption: Supine with the table broken and slight head-down tilt; the stoma site marked.

med.surgx.rc-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.rc-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.rc-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.rc-step-09.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.rc-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.rc-step-10.caption: Long, healthy ureters with their blood supply are the basis of a good diversion; a cancerous margin must be found now.

med.surgx.rc-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.rc-step-11.caption: A lymphadenectomy stages the cancer and, in several cancers, controls regional disease.

med.surgx.rc-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.rc-step-12.caption: Controlling the lateral and posterior pedicles lets the bladder come out with the prostate (men) or the uterus and anterior vaginal wall (women).

med.surgx.rc-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.rc-step-14.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.rc-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.rc-step-15.caption: A 15 to 20 cm segment with good mesentery, taken away from the terminal ileum, makes a conduit that drains well.

med.surgx.rc-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.rc-step-16.caption: An anastomosis heals only if it is well perfused, tension-free and made between healthy ends.

med.surgx.rc-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.rc-step-17.caption: Tension-free, well-vascularised joins over stents give the fewest leaks and strictures.

med.surgx.rc-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.rc-step-19.caption: A forgotten stent encrusts, obstructs and can cost the kidney.

med.surgx.rc-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.rc-step-20.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.rc-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.rc-step-21.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.rc-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.rc-step-22.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.rc-step-23.title: Step 23
med.surgx.rc-step-23.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.rc-step-24.title: Step 24
med.surgx.rc-step-24.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.nu-step-07.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.nu-step-08.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.
