med.surgx.nu-step-09.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.nu-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.nu-step-13.caption: The kidney, perinephric fat and ureter come out as one oncological block.

med.surgx.nu-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.nu-step-14.caption: The intramural ureter and its orifice can carry tumour.

med.surgx.nu-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.nu-step-16.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.nu-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.nu-step-17.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.nu-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.nu-step-19.caption: After urethral or bladder surgery the catheter splints the repair.

med.surgx.nu-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.nu-step-20.caption: One dose of chemotherapy into the bladder after surgery reduces the chance of a bladder recurrence.

med.surgx.nu-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.nu-step-21.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.nu-step-23.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.fcs-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.fcs-step-10.caption: A stent left in too long encrusts and can block or break.

med.surgx.fcs-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.fcs-step-11.caption: A flexible look is for diagnosis.

med.surgx.fcs-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.fcs-step-12.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.dviu-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.dviu-step-09.caption: The safety wire is the road home.

med.surgx.dviu-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.dviu-step-10.caption: Cutting the scar at 12 o'clock releases the narrowing with the least bleeding and keeps away from the rectum and the corpora at the sides.

med.surgx.dviu-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.dviu-step-11.caption: A blind cut makes a false passage that turns a simple stricture into a complex one.

med.surgx.clp-step-07.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.clp-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.clp-step-08.caption: Breaking the stone is the point of the operation, but the energy that breaks stone also cuts urothelium, guidewires and scopes.

med.surgx.clp-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.clp-step-09.caption: Residual fragments grow, cause colic and bring the patient back.

med.surgx.clp-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.clp-step-10.caption: Bladder stones usually form behind outflow obstruction or in stagnant urine.

med.surgx.clp-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.clp-step-11.caption: A perforation recognised in theatre changes the plan and is usually manageable; one recognised in recovery presents as abdominal distension, pain and fluid overload, and costs time the patient may not have.

med.surgx.holep-step-07.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.holep-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.holep-step-08.caption: A holmium laser damages eyes and burns drapes.

med.surgx.holep-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.holep-step-09.caption: The adenoma peels off the surgical capsule like an orange segment.

med.surgx.holep-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.holep-step-10.caption: Following the capsule all the way round leaves a smooth, wide channel with little residual tissue.

med.surgx.holep-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.holep-step-12.caption: The morcellator blades suck in anything they touch.

med.surgx.holep-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.holep-step-13.caption: A morcellator injury can perforate the bladder.

med.surgx.holep-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.holep-step-14.caption: A perforation recognised in theatre changes the plan and is usually manageable; one recognised in recovery presents as abdominal distension, pain and fluid overload, and costs time the patient may not have.

med.surgx.holep-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.holep-step-15.caption: After a resection the bladder must stay empty and free of clot while the raw surface stops oozing.

med.surgx.holep-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.holep-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.vas-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.vas-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.vas-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.vas-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.vas-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.vas-step-03.caption: Supine, the penis taped up onto the abdomen, only the scrotum exposed.

med.surgx.vas-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.vas-step-04.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.vas-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.vas-step-05.caption: Holding the vas firmly under the skin at one spot makes the procedure short and keeps the vessels out of the way.

med.surgx.vas-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.vas-step-06.caption: A vasal block numbs the vas and its sheath; a skin weal alone is not enough.

med.surgx.vas-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.vas-step-07.caption: A small puncture with sharp forceps heals without stitches and causes fewer haematomas than a scalpel incision.

med.surgx.vas-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.vas-step-12.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.vas-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.vas-step-13.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.urp-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.urp-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.urp-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.urp-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.urp-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.urp-step-03.caption: Instrumenting infected urine can cause urosepsis within hours.

med.surgx.urp-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.urp-step-04.caption: Antibiotic before incision plus VTE prophylaxis.

med.surgx.urp-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.urp-step-05.caption: Lithotomy, legs well padded; a nasal tube so the mouth is free.

med.surgx.urp-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.urp-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.urp-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.urp-step-07.caption: Every endoscopic bladder operation starts with a complete map.

med.surgx.urp-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.urp-step-08.caption: Inner cheek mucosa is wet, thick and takes well.

med.surgx.urp-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.urp-step-10.caption: Recurrence comes from scar left at the ends.

med.surgx.urp-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.urp-step-11.caption: The graft lives on its bed in the first days.

med.surgx.urp-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.urp-step-12.caption: After urethral or bladder surgery the catheter splints the repair.

med.surgx.urp-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.urp-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.urp-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.urp-step-16.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ldn-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ldn-step-12.caption: The left renal vein's tributaries (adrenal, gonadal, lumbar) must be divided to give length, and a missed lumbar vein tears when the kidney is lifted.

med.surgx.pyelo-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.pyelo-step-12.caption: Removing the narrow segment and opening the ureter along its side makes a wide, funnel-shaped join.

med.surgx.pn-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.pn-step-11.caption: The tumour's deep edge is not visible.

med.surgx.pn-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.pn-step-13.caption: A thin rim of normal kidney around the tumour gives a clear margin without wasting kidney.

med.surgx.pn-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.pn-step-15.caption: The kidney must pink up and stop bleeding.

med.surgx.pn-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.pn-step-17.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.rp-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.rp-step-18.caption: A leak found on the table is fixed with one stitch; a leak found on day three is a urinoma, ileus and a longer catheter.

med.surgx.rp-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.rp-step-19.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.rp-step-24.title: Step 24
med.surgx.rp-step-24.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.rc-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.rc-step-08.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.rc-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.rc-step-13.caption: The axillary and internal jugular veins form the boundaries of the commonest nodal clearances.

med.surgx.nu-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.nu-step-10.caption: Tumour cells shed into the wound, the peritoneum or a port site produce a recurrence that no adjuvant therapy fully reverses.

med.surgx.nu-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.nu-step-11.caption: Clipping below the tumour before handling the kidney stops tumour cells being pushed into the bladder.

med.surgx.nu-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.nu-step-12.caption: Securing the artery first stops the kidney swelling with blood when the vein is closed.

med.surgx.nu-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.nu-step-15.caption: A leak found on the table is fixed with one stitch; a leak found on day three is a urinoma, ileus and a longer catheter.

med.surgx.nu-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.nu-step-18.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.mx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.mx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.mx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.mx-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.mx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.mx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.mx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.mx-step-05.caption: Supine with the head turned away from the operative ear on a head ring, the mastoid uppermost.

med.surgx.mx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.mx-step-06.caption: Facial nerve monitoring helps the surgeon find and follow the nerve, but only if it works.

med.surgx.mx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.mx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.mx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.mx-step-08.caption: Ear and laryngeal surgery is done at high magnification with millimetre margins.

med.surgx.mx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.mx-step-09.caption: Nasal and ear surgery is done through a small opening under magnification, where a few drops of blood hide the plane, the nerve or the flap edge.

med.surgx.mx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.mx-step-10.caption: The postaural approach gives a wide view of the mastoid cortex and the posterior canal, and the same incision yields temporalis fascia, the commonest graft for the drum.

med.surgx.mx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.mx-step-11.caption: The drill removes bone a fraction of a millimetre from the facial nerve, the dura, the sigmoid sinus and the inner ear.

med.surgx.mx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.mx-step-14.caption: Residual matrix becomes recurrent disease, but matrix stripped off the stapes footplate or a fistula can cost the patient their hearing and balance.

med.surgx.mx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.mx-step-15.caption: Each of these is survivable when recognised and handled calmly at the time, and dangerous when it is hidden or chased with the drill.

med.surgx.mx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.mx-step-16.caption: In a canal wall down operation, a graft rebuilds a closed, aerated middle ear for hearing, and the meatoplasty decides whether the cavity can be seen and cleaned for the rest of the patient's life.

med.surgx.mx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.mx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.mx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.mx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.mx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.mx-step-21.caption: A facial weakness found the next morning cannot be dated: it may be an immediate injury that needs urgent re-exploration, or delayed oedema that usually recovers.

med.surgx.mx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.mx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.tux-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.tux-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.tux-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.tux-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.tux-step-05.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.tux-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.tux-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.tux-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.tux-step-08.caption: Ear and laryngeal surgery is done at high magnification with millimetre margins.

med.surgx.tux-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.tux-step-09.caption: Nasal and ear surgery is done through a small opening under magnification, where a few drops of blood hide the plane, the nerve or the flap edge.

med.surgx.tux-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.tux-step-11.caption: A perforation persists because its edge has healed as a rim of squamous epithelium.

med.surgx.tux-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.tux-step-12.caption: The flap gives access to the middle ear without enlarging the perforation, and carries the annulus that will hold the graft.

med.surgx.tux-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.tux-step-13.caption: The drill removes bone a fraction of a millimetre from the facial nerve, the dura, the sigmoid sinus and the inner ear.

med.surgx.tux-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.tux-step-14.caption: A type 1 tympanoplasty only restores hearing if the chain conducts.

med.surgx.tux-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.tux-step-15.caption: A tympanoplasty that covers cholesteatoma hides it under a healthy-looking drum until it has eroded further.

med.surgx.tux-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.tux-step-16.caption: An underlay graft sits medial to the drum remnant, supported from below, so the remnant's raw edge grows across it.

med.surgx.tux-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.tux-step-17.caption: The tympanomeatal flap holds the posterior graft edge in place and covers bare bone.

med.surgx.tux-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.tux-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.tux-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.tux-step-20.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.tux-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.tux-step-21.caption: A facial weakness found the next morning cannot be dated: it may be an immediate injury that needs urgent re-exploration, or delayed oedema that usually recovers.

med.surgx.tux-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.tux-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.spx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.spx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.spx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.spx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.spx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.spx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.spx-step-05.caption: Supine with a head ring and a shoulder roll, the head turned away from the operative side and extended moderately.

med.surgx.spx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.spx-step-06.caption: Facial nerve monitoring helps the surgeon find and follow the nerve, but only if it works.

med.surgx.spx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.spx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.spx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.spx-step-08.caption: The incision must give access to the trunk behind and the branches in front while staying in natural creases.

med.surgx.spx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.spx-step-09.caption: The facial nerve trunk can only be found once the tail and back of the gland are freed from the sternocleidomastoid and the ear canal cartilage, and the posterior belly of digastric is seen.

med.surgx.spx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.spx-step-10.caption: Everything that follows is dissected from the trunk forwards.

med.surgx.spx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.spx-step-11.caption: The superficial lobe is removed by following the nerve and its branches, dividing only the gland that lies superficial to them.

med.surgx.spx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.spx-step-12.caption: Tumour cells shed into the wound, the peritoneum or a port site produce a recurrence that no adjuvant therapy fully reverses.

med.surgx.spx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.spx-step-13.caption: Some tumours sit over the trunk, and revision surgery distorts the landmarks.

med.surgx.spx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.spx-step-14.caption: A nerve that responds to stimulation at the trunk at the end of the operation is very likely to recover even if the face is weak afterwards.

med.surgx.spx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.spx-step-15.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.spx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.spx-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.spx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.spx-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.spx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.spx-step-20.caption: A facial weakness found the next morning cannot be dated: it may be an immediate injury that needs urgent re-exploration, or delayed oedema that usually recovers.

med.surgx.spx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.spx-step-21.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.mbx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.mbx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.mbx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.mbx-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.mbx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.mbx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.mbx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.mbx-step-05.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.mbx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.mbx-step-06.caption: Supine with the neck flexed on the chest and the head extended at the atlanto-occipital joint (the sniffing position), on a head ring with a pillow or adjustable headrest.

med.surgx.mbx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.mbx-step-07.caption: Gags and laryngoscopes lever against the upper teeth, and dental injury is one of the commonest reasons ENT patients complain.

med.surgx.mbx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.mbx-step-08.caption: Exposure of the larynx is achieved by lifting the tongue and hyoid forward along the laryngoscope's axis.

med.surgx.mbx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.mbx-step-09.caption: The MDT stages the tumour from this examination.

med.surgx.mbx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.mbx-step-10.caption: Suspension frees both hands for microsurgery and gives a stable view under the microscope.

med.surgx.mbx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.mbx-step-11.caption: Ear and laryngeal surgery is done at high magnification with millimetre margins.

med.surgx.mbx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.mbx-step-15.caption: A retained throat pack or a clot in the nasopharynx sitting above the larynx can obstruct the airway completely after extubation.

med.surgx.mbx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.mbx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.mbx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.mbx-step-18.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.mbx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.mbx-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.dhsx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.dhsx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.dhsx-step-04.caption: Supine on a traction table with a well-padded perineal post.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.dhsx-step-05.caption: Fixation is only as good as the images it is judged by, and every second of screening is dose to the patient and the team.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.dhsx-step-06.caption: Fixing a malreduced fracture fixes the malreduction.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.dhsx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.dhsx-step-08.caption: The lateral approach reaches the lateral cortex through a single muscle with no internervous plane needed, and it is extensile if the plan changes.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.dhsx-step-09.caption: Reamers, screws and nails follow the guidewire.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.dhsx-step-10.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.dhsx-step-11.caption: The lag screw is the fixation.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.dhsx-step-12.caption: The barrel lets the head-neck fragment slide and impact onto the shaft.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.dhsx-step-13.caption: The final images are the evidence of what was achieved.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.dhsx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.dhsx-step-16.title: Step 16

med.surgx.tinx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.tinx-step-05.caption: Fixation is only as good as the images it is judged by, and every second of screening is dose to the patient and the team.

med.surgx.tinx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.tinx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.tinx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.tinx-step-08.caption: Fixing a malreduced fracture fixes the malreduction.

med.surgx.tinx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.tinx-step-09.caption: Reamers, screws and nails follow the guidewire.

med.surgx.tinx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.tinx-step-10.caption: Reaming allows a larger, stiffer nail.

med.surgx.tinx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.tinx-step-11.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.tinx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.tinx-step-12.caption: Locking controls length and rotation; inserting the nail without losing reduction is what makes the locking worth doing.

med.surgx.tinx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.tinx-step-13.caption: The final images are the evidence of what was achieved.

med.surgx.tinx-step-15.title: Step 15

med.surgx.tinx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.tinx-step-16.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.tinx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.tinx-step-17.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.ofdx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ofdx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.ofdx-step-04.caption: Supine on a radiolucent table with the limb free and supported.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ofdx-step-05.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ofdx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ofdx-step-07.caption: Photographs let the next surgeon see the wound without taking the dressing down, and they document the injury and what was done to it.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ofdx-step-08.caption: Incisions placed on the fasciotomy lines decompress the compartments and preserve the perforators on which later local flaps depend.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ofdx-step-09.caption: Antibiotics do not reach dead tissue.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ofdx-step-10.caption: Dead muscle left behind becomes infection and drives rhabdomyolysis; healthy muscle removed is function lost.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ofdx-step-11.caption: Devitalised bone is a sequestrum in waiting.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ofdx-step-12.caption: Irrigation dilutes what debridement cannot pick out.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ofdx-step-13.caption: Once debridement is complete, anything implanted or reconstructed at the same sitting should be done as clean surgery, not with the instruments that handled the contamination.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ofdx-step-14.caption: Fixation is only as good as the images it is judged by, and every second of screening is dose to the patient and the team.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ofdx-step-15.caption: Fixing a malreduced fracture fixes the malreduction.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.ofdx-step-16.caption: The wrong size, side or type cannot be undone after insertion, and an implant that is not registered cannot be traced if it is recalled.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.ofdx-step-17.caption: A frame holds length and alignment while the soft tissues declare themselves, without placing metal in a contaminated wound.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.ofdx-step-18.caption: The final images are the evidence of what was achieved.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.ofdx-step-20.caption: A wound that dries out or is repeatedly undressed loses tissue and gains bacteria.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.ofdx-step-21.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.ofdx-step-22.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.ofdx-step-23.title: Step 23
med.surgx.ofdx-step-23.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lfx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lfx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lfx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lfx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lfx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lfx-step-04.caption: Supine, with the leg supported so both medial and lateral sides are accessible.

med.surgx.lfx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lfx-step-05.caption: A tourniquet gives a bloodless field but adds ischaemia to injured tissue and hides bleeding that tells you what is alive.

med.surgx.lfx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lfx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lfx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lfx-step-08.caption: One lateral incision over the intermuscular septum releases both the anterior and the lateral compartments, provided the septum is found first.

med.surgx.lfx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lfx-step-09.caption: The deep posterior compartment is the one that is missed, and it contains the posterior tibial vessels and tibial nerve.

med.surgx.lfx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lfx-step-10.caption: Dead muscle left behind becomes infection and drives rhabdomyolysis; healthy muscle removed is function lost.

med.surgx.lfx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lfx-step-11.caption: Antibiotics do not reach dead tissue.

med.surgx.lfx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lfx-step-12.caption: Photographs let the next surgeon see the wound without taking the dressing down, and they document the injury and what was done to it.

med.surgx.lfx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lfx-step-14.caption: A wound that dries out or is repeatedly undressed loses tissue and gains bacteria.

med.surgx.lfx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lfx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lfx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lfx-step-16.caption: Deficits and compartment syndrome that are found early are treatable.

med.surgx.lfx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lfx-step-17.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.qdx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.qdx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.qdx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.qdx-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.qdx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.qdx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.qdx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.qdx-step-04.caption: Sitting upright on a couch or chair with the head supported against a headrest or held by an assistant, chin slightly down.

med.surgx.qdx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.qdx-step-05.caption: Local anaesthetic works poorly in the acidic tissue of an abscess, which is why patients remember these procedures.

med.surgx.qdx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.qdx-step-06.caption: The abscess is usually at the superior pole, and the carotid is lateral.

med.surgx.qdx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.qdx-step-07.caption: Needle aspiration confirms the diagnosis and often drains the abscess on its own.

med.surgx.qdx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.qdx-step-08.caption: Pus obtained at drainage is the specimen that guides therapy.

med.surgx.qdx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.qdx-step-09.caption: Aspiration alone often suffices, but a large or thick-walled collection drains better through an incision.

med.surgx.qdx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.qdx-step-10.caption: An abscess that is not fully de-loculated is an abscess that has been partly drained, and it is the commonest reason for recurrence and readmission.

med.surgx.qdx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.qdx-step-11.caption: A dry tap may mean peritonsillar cellulitis, an abscess in a different position, or deep neck space disease.

med.surgx.qdx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.qdx-step-13.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.qdx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.qdx-step-15.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.mcx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.mcx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.mcx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.mcx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.mcx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.mcx-step-03.caption: Gynaecological and obstetric operations rest on a scan, a test result and a plan agreed in clinic.

med.surgx.mcx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.mcx-step-05.caption: Lithotomy; slight head-down tilt helps when membranes are bulging.

med.surgx.mcx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.mcx-step-06.caption: The size, position and mobility of the uterus and the state of the cervix under anaesthesia decide the direction of every instrument that follows.

med.surgx.mcx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.mcx-step-07.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.mcx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.mcx-step-08.caption: The suture can only be placed high if the cervicovaginal junction is seen all the way round, and a soft pregnant cervix tears if it is held with toothed instruments.

med.surgx.mcx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.mcx-step-09.caption: In rescue cerclage the membranes may prolapse through the os.

med.surgx.mcx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.mcx-step-10.caption: A cerclage helps only if it is high on the cervix.

med.surgx.mcx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.mcx-step-11.caption: The knot must close the os without cutting through the cervix, and the suture must be easy to find and cut in labour or at 36 to 37 weeks.

med.surgx.mcx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.mcx-step-13.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.mcx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.mcx-step-14.caption: The operation is for the pregnancy.

med.surgx.mcx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.mcx-step-15.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ax-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.ax-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.ax-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ax-step-02.caption: ENT operations are often elective and sided, and each rests on one investigation: the audiogram and tympanogram for grommets, the CT for sinus surgery, the documented infection count or sleep study for tonsillectomy.

med.surgx.ax-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.ax-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ax-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ax-step-05.caption: In ENT surgery the surgeon and the anaesthetist work in the same space.

med.surgx.ax-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ax-step-07.caption: Gags and laryngoscopes lever against the upper teeth, and dental injury is one of the commonest reasons ENT patients complain.

med.surgx.ax-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ax-step-08.caption: A submucous cleft is easy to miss by looking and easy to find by feeling.

med.surgx.ax-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ax-step-09.caption: Adenoid tissue in the choanae and around the tori is what causes persisting obstruction and ear disease, and it cannot be judged by feel.

med.surgx.ax-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ax-step-10.caption: The aim is a clear airway and choanae with the tori, the prevertebral tissue and the velopharyngeal fringe intact.

med.surgx.ax-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ax-step-11.caption: After curettage most bleeding is from raw lymphoid tissue and stops with pressure.

med.surgx.ax-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.ax-step-13.caption: Persistent nasopharyngeal bleeding in a small child becomes a volume problem quickly, and the blood loss is hidden because it is swallowed.

med.surgx.ax-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ax-step-14.caption: A retained throat pack or a clot in the nasopharynx sitting above the larynx can obstruct the airway completely after extubation.

med.surgx.ax-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.ax-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ax-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.ax-step-17.caption: Most ENT airway catastrophes happen after the operation, in recovery or on the ward, in the hands of people who were not in theatre.

med.surgx.ax-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.ax-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.mx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.mx-step-12.caption: Every mastoid operation starts here, and the order matters.

med.surgx.mx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.mx-step-13.caption: A canal wall down operation turns the mastoid, attic and canal into one cavity that can be inspected for life.

med.surgx.tux-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.tux-step-10.caption: The postaural approach gives a wide view of the mastoid cortex and the posterior canal, and the same incision yields temporalis fascia, the commonest graft for the drum.

med.surgx.mbx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.mbx-step-12.caption: A suspected cancer needs tissue deep enough to show invasion, from the living edge of the tumour.

med.surgx.adx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.adx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.adx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.adx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.adx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.adx-step-03.caption: Position so the incision lies at the most dependent point of the cavity.

med.surgx.adx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.adx-step-04.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.adx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.adx-step-05.caption: Local anaesthetic works poorly in the acidic tissue of an abscess, which is why patients remember these procedures.

med.surgx.adx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.adx-step-06.caption: The incision must be long enough and placed so the cavity drains with gravity, or the abscess reforms and the patient returns.

med.surgx.adx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.adx-step-07.caption: Pus obtained at drainage is the specimen that guides therapy.

med.surgx.adx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.adx-step-08.caption: An abscess that is not fully de-loculated is an abscess that has been partly drained, and it is the commonest reason for recurrence and readmission.

med.surgx.adx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.adx-step-09.caption: An abscess cavity closed primarily becomes an abscess again.

med.surgx.adx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.adx-step-11.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.hpx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.hpx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.hpx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.hpx-step-02.caption: Most stoma leaks, skin problems and appliance failures trace back to where the stoma was put.

med.surgx.hpx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.hpx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.hpx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.hpx-step-07.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.hpx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.hpx-step-08.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.hpx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.hpx-step-09.caption: Bowel handled roughly becomes ileus, adhesions and, at the extreme, a serosal tear that becomes a leak.

med.surgx.hpx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.hpx-step-10.caption: The left ureter is injured during sigmoid mobilisation when the surgeon dissects in an inflamed field without first finding it.

med.surgx.hpx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.hpx-step-13.caption: Division is where contamination of the field happens.

med.surgx.hpx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.hpx-step-14.caption: Removing contamination is part of source control, but lavage does not substitute for closing the hole that produced it.

med.surgx.hpx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.hpx-step-16.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.hpx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.hpx-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.hpx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.hpx-step-19.caption: The trephine is a hole in the abdominal wall that must be large enough to keep the stoma perfused and small enough not to become a parastomal hernia.

med.surgx.hpx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.hpx-step-20.caption: A badly sited stoma is a lifelong problem for the patient and a daily one for the stoma nurse.

med.surgx.hpx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.hpx-step-21.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.hpx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.hpx-step-22.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.hpx-step-24.title: Step 24
med.surgx.hpx-step-24.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lix-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lix-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lix-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lix-step-02.caption: Most stoma leaks, skin problems and appliance failures trace back to where the stoma was put.

med.surgx.lix-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.lix-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lix-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lix-step-05.caption: Supine, or modified Lloyd-Davies when the ileostomy is formed as part of a pelvic operation.

med.surgx.lix-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lix-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lix-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lix-step-07.caption: The loop must defunction what lies distal to it, reach the skin without tension and be closable later.

med.surgx.lix-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lix-step-08.caption: The trephine is a hole in the abdominal wall that must be large enough to keep the stoma perfused and small enough not to become a parastomal hernia.

med.surgx.lix-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lix-step-09.caption: Delivery without twisting and without tearing the mesentery keeps the stoma perfused and functional.

med.surgx.lix-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lix-step-11.caption: Closure is often taught as a minor operation, but most of its complications come from this step: enterotomies made while freeing a stoma that is densely adherent to fascia and peritoneum.

med.surgx.lix-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lix-step-12.caption: An anastomosis heals only if it is well perfused, tension-free and made between healthy ends.

med.surgx.lix-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lix-step-13.caption: A handsewn anastomosis adapts to bowel of mismatched calibre, to thick oedematous wall and to settings without a stapler.

med.surgx.lix-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lix-step-14.caption: A defect found on the table costs a stitch.

med.surgx.lix-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lix-step-17.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lix-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lix-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lix-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.lix-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lpdux-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lpdux-step-04.caption: Supine, French position (legs apart) or American, with reverse Trendelenburg for the upper abdomen and Trendelenburg later for pelvic washout.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lpdux-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lpdux-step-06.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lpdux-step-08.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lpdux-step-10.caption: A perforated ulcer edge is inflamed and holds sutures poorly.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lpdux-step-11.caption: A defect found on the table costs a stitch.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lpdux-step-12.caption: Laparoscopy is a means to a good repair and a thorough washout, not an end.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lpdux-step-13.caption: Removing contamination is part of source control, but lavage does not substitute for closing the hole that produced it.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lpdux-step-14.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lpdux-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lpdux-step-18.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lpdux-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lpdux-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.lpdux-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.sbrx-step-06.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.sbrx-step-07.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.sbrx-step-08.caption: Bowel handled roughly becomes ileus, adhesions and, at the extreme, a serosal tear that becomes a leak.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.sbrx-step-09.caption: Every centimetre resected unnecessarily may matter later, and every centimetre of dead bowel left behind will perforate.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.sbrx-step-10.caption: The mesenteric division decides the blood supply of both cut ends.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.sbrx-step-11.caption: Division is where contamination of the field happens.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.sbrx-step-12.caption: An anastomosis heals only if it is well perfused, tension-free and made between healthy ends.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.sbrx-step-13.caption: A handsewn anastomosis adapts to bowel of mismatched calibre, to thick oedematous wall and to settings without a stapler.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.sbrx-step-14.caption: An open mesenteric window can trap a loop of small bowel and cause an internal hernia.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.sbrx-step-15.caption: A defect found on the table costs a stitch.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.sbrx-step-16.caption: The residual length, the presence of the ileocaecal valve and continuity with the colon predict the risk of intestinal failure.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.sbrx-step-17.caption: Removing contamination is part of source control, but lavage does not substitute for closing the hole that produced it.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.sbrx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.sbrx-step-21.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.sbrx-step-22.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.sbrx-step-23.title: Step 23
med.surgx.sbrx-step-23.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lihrx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lihrx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lihrx-step-04.caption: Supine, both arms tucked at the sides so the surgeon and camera holder can stand on the opposite side to the hernia.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lihrx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lihrx-step-06.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lihrx-step-08.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lihrx-step-09.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lihrx-step-10.caption: The flap opens the preperitoneal space from inside and must later cover the mesh completely.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lihrx-step-11.caption: From behind, the groin is a different anatomy.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lihrx-step-12.caption: Conversion is a safe outcome, not a failure.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lihrx-step-13.caption: Most hernia complications start with the sac: contents injured during reduction, non-viable bowel returned to the abdomen, or a sac left partly unreduced that becomes the recurrence.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lihrx-step-14.caption: The lower edge of the mesh can only lie flat if the peritoneum is lifted well off the vas and gonadal vessels.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lihrx-step-15.caption: A bowel injury or unexpected contamination changes the operation.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lihrx-step-16.caption: Mesh repair halves recurrence compared with suture alone for most hernias, but only when the mesh is large enough, lies flat in the chosen plane and stays clean.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lihrx-step-17.caption: The mesh must cover the whole myopectoral orifice, direct, indirect and femoral spaces, with overlap.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lihrx-step-18.caption: Exposed mesh adheres to bowel, and a gap in the peritoneal closure can trap a loop of bowel.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lihrx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.lihrx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lihrx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.lihrx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-04.caption: Supine, arms out, with the abdomen exposed from the costal margins to the pubis for an incisional hernia.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-06.caption: The incision has to reach healthy fascia in every direction around the defect and must not devascularise the skin.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-07.caption: Most hernia complications start with the sac: contents injured during reduction, non-viable bowel returned to the abdomen, or a sac left partly unreduced that becomes the recurrence.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-08.caption: A bowel injury or unexpected contamination changes the operation.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-09.caption: The repair is chosen after the fascia is defined, not from the clinic note.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-10.caption: The retromuscular space between the rectus muscle and the posterior sheath is well vascularised and separated from the bowel, so a mesh there is protected and integrates well.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-11.caption: The posterior sheath and peritoneum separate the mesh from the bowel.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-12.caption: Mesh repair halves recurrence compared with suture alone for most hernias, but only when the mesh is large enough, lies flat in the chosen plane and stays clean.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-14.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-16.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-17.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-19.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.ovhrx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.ovhrx-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lisx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.lisx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.lisx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.lisx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lisx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lisx-step-04.caption: Lithotomy or prone jack-knife; record which.

med.surgx.lisx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.lisx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lisx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lisx-step-06.caption: Local infiltration with a vasoconstrictor reduces bleeding, opens tissue planes and lowers early post-operative pain and opioid use, and it allows many anorectal operations to be done as day cases with less urinary retention.

med.surgx.lisx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lisx-step-07.caption: The pre-operative diagnosis in anorectal surgery is often made in an awake patient in pain.

med.surgx.lisx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lisx-step-09.caption: Anorectal operations are elective and the sphincter does not regrow.

med.surgx.lisx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lisx-step-14.caption: Bleeding, an over-tight canal and a missed second lesion are all visible at the end of the operation and invisible once the patient is awake and the swelling starts.

med.surgx.lisx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lisx-step-15.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lisx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lisx-step-17.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lisx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lisx-step-18.caption: Most anorectal and pilonidal wounds are left open or are under tension during defaecation.

med.surgx.lisx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lisx-step-19.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.psex-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.psex-step-04.caption: Prone jack-knife with the hips flexed.

med.surgx.psex-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.psex-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.psex-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.psex-step-06.caption: Recurrence after pilonidal surgery usually comes from a pit or a lateral tract that was not included.

med.surgx.psex-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.psex-step-07.caption: Local infiltration with a vasoconstrictor reduces bleeding, opens tissue planes and lowers early post-operative pain and opioid use, and it allows many anorectal operations to be done as day cases with less urinary retention.

med.surgx.psex-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.psex-step-08.caption: The aim is to remove all diseased pits and tracts with as little healthy tissue as possible.

med.surgx.psex-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.psex-step-09.caption: The choice of wound management decides healing time and recurrence.

med.surgx.psex-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.psex-step-11.caption: An off-midline closure works by flattening the natal cleft and placing the scar away from the midline, where friction, moisture and hair drive recurrence.

med.surgx.psex-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.psex-step-12.caption: A flap closed under tension, over hidden infection or with doubtful blood supply breaks down, and a failed closure heals more slowly than a wound left open from the start.

med.surgx.psex-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.psex-step-13.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.psex-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.psex-step-14.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.psex-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.psex-step-16.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.psex-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.psex-step-17.caption: Most anorectal and pilonidal wounds are left open or are under tension during defaecation.

med.surgx.psex-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.psex-step-18.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.lnfx-step-04.caption: Supine in steep reverse Trendelenburg, with legs apart (French position) or the surgeon on the patient's right, according to unit practice.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.lnfx-step-06.caption: Access is where laparoscopy injures people.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lnfx-step-07.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lnfx-step-08.caption: The hiatus lies behind the left lateral segment of the liver.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lnfx-step-09.caption: The fundus has to be free to wrap without tension, and in a sleeve gastrectomy the whole greater curvature must be mobilised so no fundus is left behind.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lnfx-step-10.caption: Hiatal dissection is where the vagi, the pleura, the aorta and the oesophagus are injured.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lnfx-step-11.caption: Most hernia complications start with the sac: contents injured during reduction, non-viable bowel returned to the abdomen, or a sac left partly unreduced that becomes the recurrence.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lnfx-step-12.caption: A wrap placed under tension on a short oesophagus pulls up into the chest.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lnfx-step-13.caption: Conversion is a safe outcome, not a failure.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lnfx-step-14.caption: The bougie sets the calibre of the wrap or the sleeve, and its passage is a recognised cause of oesophageal and gastric perforation.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lnfx-step-15.caption: Recurrent hiatal herniation is the commonest anatomical failure of antireflux and bariatric surgery.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lnfx-step-16.caption: The wrap restores a high-pressure zone at the gastro-oesophageal junction.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.lnfx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lnfx-step-19.caption: A port-site hernia through an unclosed 10 mm fascial defect can strangulate, and it presents days later to someone who was not in theatre.

med.surgx.lnfx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.lnfx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-14.caption: The staple line decides the shape of the sleeve and where it fails.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lsgx-step-15.caption: Conversion is a safe outcome, not a failure.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.lsgx-step-16.caption: A defect found on the table costs a stitch.

med.surgx.lsgx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-05.title: Step 5

med.surgx.lhsx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.lhsx-step-07.caption: Ports placed for the anatomy you have, rather than for the textbook, are the difference between a comfortable operation and a fight.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.lhsx-step-08.caption: The first look answers a question the imaging could not, and it is the only chance to find the second diagnosis before attention narrows to the first.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lhsx-step-09.caption: Lifting the sigmoid and descending mesocolon off the retroperitoneum in the embryological plane keeps the lymphatic envelope intact and keeps the left ureter, gonadal vessels and hypogastric nerves behind the plane.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lhsx-step-10.caption: The level of the vascular tie sets the lymph node yield for a cancer, the reach of the colon to the pelvis, and the blood supply of the proximal limb.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lhsx-step-11.caption: A colorectal anastomosis must lie in the pelvis without tension.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.lhsx-step-13.caption: Bringing an infected or neoplastic specimen through the abdominal wall unprotected causes port-site infection and, in malignancy, port-site recurrence.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.lhsx-step-14.caption: Division is where contamination of the field happens.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.lhsx-step-17.caption: A colorectal anastomotic leak is the complication that kills after this operation.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.lhsx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.lhsx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.lhsx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.lhsx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.oscx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.oscx-step-02.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.oscx-step-04.title: Step 4
med.surgx.oscx-step-04.caption: Supine, with the right side of the abdomen accessible and arms out on boards abducted no more than 90 degrees.

med.surgx.oscx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.oscx-step-05.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.oscx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.oscx-step-06.caption: Upper abdominal organs sit high under the costal margin.

med.surgx.oscx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.oscx-step-08.caption: Starting at the fundus, away from the inflamed triangle, lets the gallbladder be separated from the liver in a plane that is easier to find.

med.surgx.oscx-step-09.caption: A cholangiogram shows the anatomy of the ducts and any stones within them.

med.surgx.oscx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.oscx-step-10.caption: Bile duct injuries are rarely technical slips; they are decisions to continue when the anatomy is not clear.

med.surgx.oscx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.oscx-step-14.caption: The outcome of a bile duct injury depends more on what happens next than on the injury itself.

med.surgx.oscx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.oscx-step-15.caption: Bile leaks are among the commonest complications of biliary and liver surgery.

med.surgx.oscx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.oscx-step-16.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.lcex-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.lcex-step-09.caption: A cholangiogram shows the anatomy of the ducts and any stones within them.

med.surgx.lcex-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.lcex-step-10.caption: The transcystic route leaves the common duct intact and avoids a duct closure, so it has fewer bile leaks and strictures.

med.surgx.lcex-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.lcex-step-11.caption: Working through the cystic duct uses an opening that will be ligated anyway, so clearance can be achieved without any incision in the common duct.

med.surgx.lcex-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.lcex-step-12.caption: A short vertical incision on the front of the supraduodenal duct avoids the axial arteries at 3 and 9 o'clock and can be closed without narrowing the duct.

med.surgx.lcex-step-13.title: Step 13

med.surgx.lcex-step-14.caption: The closure must be watertight without narrowing the duct.

med.surgx.lcex-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.lcex-step-15.caption: An uncleared duct is not a failure if it is left safe.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-04.caption: Trauma: supine, arms out, prepared from nipples to knees for a full trauma laparotomy.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-06.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-07.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-08.caption: The splenic hilum is deep and posterior.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-09.caption: Preserving the spleen avoids lifelong infection risk, but a repair that bleeds again in an unstable patient is lethal.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-10.caption: The short gastrics tether the spleen to the greater curve.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-11.caption: The hilum carries the splenic artery and vein and lies against the tail of the pancreas.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-12.caption: In upper abdominal surgery the large veins (portal, superior mesenteric, splenic, hepatic and the cava) tear rather than cut, and clamping blindly makes a small hole large.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-13.caption: An accessory spleen left behind after splenectomy for immune thrombocytopenia or haemolysis can enlarge and cause relapse.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.splenectomy-step-15.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.splenectomy-step-20.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.lartx-step-13.caption: The lateral and anterior planes are where the circumferential margin is most often lost and where the pelvic autonomic nerves and the neurovascular bundles are injured.

med.surgx.px-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.px-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.px-step-05.caption: Supine, arms out, with a thoracic epidural or alternative analgesia per the anaesthetic plan.

med.surgx.px-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.px-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.px-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.px-step-07.caption: Upper abdominal organs sit high under the costal margin.

med.surgx.px-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.px-step-08.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.px-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.px-step-09.caption: Pre- operative imaging is a map made weeks ago.

med.surgx.px-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.px-step-10.caption: Mobilising the duodenum and pancreatic head off the inferior vena cava lets the surgeon feel the tumour between the fingers and judge its relationship to the superior mesenteric artery, and gives the posterior plane of the specimen.

med.surgx.px-step-11.title: Step 11

med.surgx.px-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.px-step-12.caption: Separating the pancreatic neck from the front of the superior mesenteric and portal veins shows whether the tumour invades them.

med.surgx.px-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.px-step-13.caption: Finding metastases or arterial encasement after the incision is common.

med.surgx.px-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.px-step-14.caption: The specimen is freed in a set order so that the last attachment, the uncinate process on the superior mesenteric artery, is dissected under full vision.

med.surgx.px-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.px-step-15.caption: The pancreatic anastomosis is the source of most serious complications.

med.surgx.px-step-16.title: Step 16

med.surgx.rhx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.rhx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.rhx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.rhx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.rhx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.rhx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.rhx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.rhx-step-05.caption: Supine, arms out, slight reverse Trendelenburg, with a bolster under the right side if helpful.

med.surgx.rhx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.rhx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.rhx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.rhx-step-08.caption: Pre-operative imaging is a map made weeks ago.

med.surgx.rhx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.rhx-step-09.caption: The right liver is held by its triangular and coronary ligaments and drained by short veins into the inferior vena cava.

med.surgx.rhx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.rhx-step-10.caption: The hepatoduodenal ligament carries the inflow of the whole liver: the bile duct, the hepatic artery and the portal vein.

med.surgx.rhx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.rhx-step-11.caption: Dividing the right-sided inflow before transection reduces bleeding and produces a visible demarcation line that marks the true plane between the right and left liver.

med.surgx.rhx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.rhx-step-12.caption: Controlling the right hepatic vein reduces back-bleeding during transection and avoids a catastrophic tear at the end of the operation.

med.surgx.rhx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.rhx-step-13.caption: Occluding the hepatoduodenal ligament stops hepatic arterial and portal inflow.

med.surgx.rhx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.rhx-step-14.caption: Transection is where most blood is lost and where the remnant's outflow and bile ducts can be injured.

med.surgx.rhx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.rhx-step-15.caption: In upper abdominal surgery the large veins (portal, superior mesenteric, splenic, hepatic and the cava) tear rather than cut, and clamping blindly makes a small hole large.

med.surgx.rhx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.rhx-step-16.caption: Bile leaks are among the commonest complications of biliary and liver surgery.

med.surgx.rhx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.rhx-step-18.caption: A drain tells you what is happening in a space you cannot see.

med.surgx.rhx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.rhx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.rhx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.rhx-step-20.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.rhx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.rhx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.mrndx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.mrndx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.mrndx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.mrndx-step-05.caption: Supine with a shoulder roll, head on a ring, turned away from the side of dissection, slight reverse Trendelenburg.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-06.title: Step 6
med.surgx.mrndx-step-06.caption: Prepare widely and drape to the field.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.mrndx-step-07.caption: The incision must give access from the mandible to the clavicle and from the midline to trapezius, while keeping skin flap blood supply intact and keeping a scar off the carotid.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.mrndx-step-08.caption: Level I drains the oral cavity and lip and must be cleared when involved or at risk.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.mrndx-step-09.caption: Preserving the accessory nerve is the main functional gain of a modified over a radical dissection.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.mrndx-step-11.caption: The nodes of levels II to IV lie along the internal jugular vein, so the specimen is peeled off the carotid sheath.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.mrndx-step-12.caption: A lymphadenectomy stages the cancer and, in several cancers, controls regional disease.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-13.title: Step 13
med.surgx.mrndx-step-13.caption: The axillary and internal jugular veins form the boundaries of the commonest nodal clearances.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.mrndx-step-14.caption: The thoracic duct and its branches enter the venous confluence at the base of level IV, especially on the left.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.mrndx-step-15.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.mrndx-step-17.caption: A nodal clearance leaves a dead space that fills with serous fluid and lymph.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-18.title: Step 18
med.surgx.mrndx-step-18.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.mrndx-step-20.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.mrndx-step-21.caption: A neck haematoma can obstruct the airway within minutes, and the people who see it first are recovery and ward staff, not the surgeon.

med.surgx.mrndx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.mrndx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.

med.surgx.dgx-step-01.title: Step 1
med.surgx.dgx-step-01.caption: Confirm identity, operation and side with the awake patient.

med.surgx.dgx-step-02.title: Step 2
med.surgx.dgx-step-02.caption: A cancer operation is one part of a treatment plan agreed by a multidisciplinary team.

med.surgx.dgx-step-03.title: Step 3
med.surgx.dgx-step-03.caption: Everyone stops and confirms before the first cut.

med.surgx.dgx-step-05.title: Step 5
med.surgx.dgx-step-05.caption: Supine, arms out, with a reverse Trendelenburg tilt available; some surgeons use legs apart (French position) for laparoscopic gastrectomy.

med.surgx.dgx-step-07.title: Step 7
med.surgx.dgx-step-07.caption: The midline is fast, bloodless and extensible in both directions, which is exactly what an unknown pathology needs.

med.surgx.dgx-step-08.title: Step 8
med.surgx.dgx-step-08.caption: The purpose of a laparotomy is to find out.

med.surgx.dgx-step-09.title: Step 9
med.surgx.dgx-step-09.caption: Peritoneal or liver metastases missed by staging, or a tumour fixed to structures that cannot be resected, mean a major resection will add risk without curing the patient.

med.surgx.dgx-step-10.title: Step 10
med.surgx.dgx-step-10.caption: The greater curve nodes (stations 4sb, 4d and 6) drain the distal stomach.

med.surgx.dgx-step-11.title: Step 11
med.surgx.dgx-step-11.caption: The suprapyloric and hepatoduodenal nodes (stations 5 and 12a) drain the antrum and pylorus, and the duodenal stump is where a leak is often fatal.

med.surgx.dgx-step-12.title: Step 12
med.surgx.dgx-step-12.caption: A lymphadenectomy stages the cancer and, in several cancers, controls regional disease.

med.surgx.dgx-step-14.title: Step 14
med.surgx.dgx-step-14.caption: The proximal margin determines whether the resection is curative, and the tumour's growth pattern sets how much margin is needed.

med.surgx.dgx-step-15.title: Step 15
med.surgx.dgx-step-15.caption: The reconstruction must carry food without bile reflux, and the anastomosis must heal.

med.surgx.dgx-step-16.title: Step 16
med.surgx.dgx-step-16.caption: After an upper gastrointestinal cancer resection, oral intake may be delayed or stopped by a leak.

med.surgx.dgx-step-17.title: Step 17
med.surgx.dgx-step-17.caption: Margin status and nodal yield are reported by the pathologist, but only from a specimen they can orient.

med.surgx.dgx-step-19.title: Step 19
med.surgx.dgx-step-19.caption: Count before closure; any discrepancy stops the closure.

med.surgx.dgx-step-20.title: Step 20
med.surgx.dgx-step-20.caption: Burst abdomen and incisional hernia are closure failures, and closure technique is one of the few variables entirely under the surgeon's control.

med.surgx.dgx-step-21.title: Step 21
med.surgx.dgx-step-21.caption: Tension-free closure with a clean dressing.

med.surgx.dgx-step-22.title: Step 22
med.surgx.dgx-step-22.caption: Write the operation note now and hand over the plan.
